maria.oncall: incident-bot paged me: p99 streaming latency breach for us-west-2 shared GPU pool. SLO p99=200ms, observed ~1.4s across many streams :rotating_light:
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency.p99 > 200ms for /v1/stream (us-west-2, pool=shared-gpu-1) — triggered at 1839999999
maria.oncall: I'm taking it. quick check: any deploys? jules?
jules: no recent deploys in the last 30m. deploy-bot shows last canary at 1839995000. nothing tagged for this pool.
kai: looking at pool metrics — saw I/O wait spike on hosts in that pool ~1839992000-1839998000. suspect noisy tenant or cgroup throttling.
chen: dumping top tenant consumers now. grabbing `runc` cgroup stats + iostat.
chen: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   r_await  w_await  %util
nvme0n1         120.5    2.3    5.3     1.1      95.2
nvme1n1         10.1     0.2    0.2     0.0      12.0
```
chen: nvme0n1 is saturated on host gpu-34. top shows a single container from tenant `acme-analytics` with huge writeback bursts.
samir: acme-analytics has been running heavy batch generation recently — they were on burst mode but shouldn't hit shared-gpu pool. checking scheduler placement.
maria.oncall: cs-echo, any customer-reported errors from AcmeCorp?
cs-echo: we have a single CS ticket marked as degraded streaming quality from ACME staging at 1839998500, marked priority P2.
kai: looking at model-serving metrics — streaming stalls correlate with KV cache evictions around the same time. eviction rate spiked 20x. implies memory pressure or KV eviction thrash.
jules: could be GPU memory pressure causing re-uploads and additional IO. cross-checking nvidia-smi on gpu-34.
jules: ```
# nvidia-smi dmon -s u
GPU    Mem%   Temp
0      92      78C
```
maria.oncall: OK pattern: one host in shared pool has NVMe saturated due to tenant writeback, causing higher IO wait -> kernel stalls -> higher tail latency for streaming. Likely noisy neighbor. Immediate mitigations?
samir: options: 1) throttle tenant IO via cgroup blkio limits; 2) evict tenant pods from shared pool and reassign to burst-dedicated; 3) drain host gpu-34 from serving with live fallback to other hosts (will add brief routing churn).
chen: blkio controls might take effect quickly. I can push a temporary throttle to acme-analytics cgroup: `echo 1048576 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/.../blkio.throttle.write_bps_device` — but need to ensure we target the right device major:minor.
kai: routing fallback + canary increase might increase tail for other hosts briefly but avoids writeback thrash. prefer safe evict for noisy tenant first.
maria.oncall: prioritize minimal customer impact. If we evict acme pods to private burst (they have dedicated burst pool entitlement), they should resume with less impact. samir, can you coordinate eviction?
samir: on it. taking policy: graceful evict (10s drain) to burst-pool-1, with forced eviction if not ready in 30s. will annotate so we can reverse.
samir: `kubectl annotate pod acme-analytics-*-* evicted-for=1839999999` then `kubectl cordon gpu-34 && kubectl drain --pod-selector=tenant=acme-analytics --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=10`
chen: while samir does that, I'm applying temporary blkio cap as belt-and-suspenders: setting acme-analytics write_bps ~100MB/s on host gpu-34.
chen: applied. iostat shows nvme0n1 write drops from 400MB/s -> 38MB/s, %util down to 22%.
kai: KV eviction rate dropping, streaming p99 trending down. current p99 ~280ms and falling. p95 back to normal.
jules: routing traces show small bump in tail for ~15s during drain but no request failures.
maria.oncall: timeline: page 1839999999, throttle and eviction started at ~1840000030, p99 back under 300ms at ~1840000065. good.
cs-echo: updated ticket with mitigation steps and ETA for final remediation. telling ACME that we saw noisy tenant interference and evicted their workload to burst.
samir: done. annotated and evicted. pods rescheduled to burst-pool-1 across us-west-2-e nodes.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE] alert resolved at 1840000105 — incident auto-close pending 30m if no regression.
maria.oncall: follow-ups: 1) reach out to tenant owner of acme-analytics — billing note and remind about burst policy; 2) add automated detection: if a tenant causes NVMe util > 80% for >2m, auto-apply blkio cap and trigger soft-evict; 3) consider moving heavy batch workloads off shared-gpu pools by default.
jules: I'll file the post-incident eval and include kernel-level metrics, nvidia mem churn, and scheduler placement logs.
chen: saving snippets of commands I ran to incidents runbook.
maria.oncall: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for 30m to watch. reactions: :thumbsup:
